To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the final mechanical properties of the steel depend on the type of phase transformation that occurs in the material during hot plastic deformation.
the mechanical properties of high-strength low alloy steel can be improved by processing the material in the γ + α area.
the mechanical properties of HSLA steel can be significantly improved through a novel thermal deformation process carried out in the (γ + α)-region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and optimization of new processing technologies for high-strength low alloy (HSLA-100) steel in order for it to attain maximum mechanical properties at its low alloy level.
the influence of hot plastic deformation in γ and ( γ + α) areas on the structure and mechanical properties of HSLA steel.
the development of new processing technology for the HSLA steel.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanical properties of HSLA steel can be improved by hot deformation processing in a two-phase region.
the HSLA steel samples that were thermally deformed at temperatures in the (γ + α ) phase field exhibited the best mechanical properties.
a new technology has been developed that allows for the production of HSLA steel with a yield strength of 700-750 MPa and an ultimate tensile strength of 800-850 MPa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical properties of HSLA steel can be improved by using a new process that includes hot deformation in a single-phase (γ)- and dual-phase (α + γ) regions.

it is possible to produce a high-strength HSLA steel with a low alloying content, by hot deformation in the γ + α area, followed by quenching and tempering, which is comparable to the mechanical properties of a high-strength steel with higher alloying content, processed using conventional schedules.
a new processing technology can be applied to HSLA steel to achieve a high strength level with a good plasticity behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microstructure of the steel is strongly dependent on the temperature of the final stage of deformation.
the microstructural changes that occur as the result of hot plastic deformation have a significant impact on the mechanical properties.
the mechanical properties of a steel depend strongly on the processing conditions, and that the mechanical properties can be improved by processing the steel in the γ and (γ+α) areas.
